title: Heterovalent 2EuII/4EuIII and Trivalent 5EuIII Clusters Assembled with a Macrocyclic Cyclen Derivative Ligand: Molecular Structures, Oxidation Stabilities, and Luminescence Properties

material_class.structural_family: heterovalent hexanuclear 2EuII/4EuIII cluster with tetrahedral 4EuIII core and cyclen-encapsulated EuII

synthesis.procedure: EuBr2 (0.062 g, 0.2 mmol) and Eu(NO3)3·6H2O (0.178 g, 0.4 mmol) were added to H4L (0.154 g, 0.2 mmol) in methanol (5 mL) under argon. Benzoic acid (0.045 g, 0.4 mmol) was then added and the mixture was stirred at room temperature for 3 min to give a clear red solution. The solution was sealed and heated at 75 °C for 12 h, then cooled to room temperature over 10 h under a controlled temperature program. Red crystals of 1 were obtained by natural evaporation of the cooled solution in air at room temperature.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature (stirring); 75 °C (solvothermal heating); cool to room temperature over 10 h
synthesis.time: stirred 3 min; heated 12 h; cooled 10 h
synthesis.vessel_or_method: sealed flask solvothermal reaction under argon
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: red crystals obtained by natural evaporation of the cooled solution in air at room temperature

properties.summary: Solid-state emission at 77 K (λexc = 360 nm) shows a strong broad band at 533 nm assigned to the Laporte-allowed 4f6 5d1 → 4f7 transition of Eu2+ plus characteristic sharp Eu3+ 5D0 → 7FJ emissions; the broad band is redshifted versus free H4L and comparable Eu2+/Eu3+ intensities are attributed to possible Eu2+→Eu3+ energy transfer. This is described as the first heterovalent europium complex clearly showing both Eu2+ and Eu3+ emission.

measurements.name: Eu3+ 5D0→7F1 emission
measurements.conditions: solid state, 77 K, λexc = 360 nm; peaks around 591, 617, 652, 698 nm for J = 1–4

synthesis.procedure: Benzoic acid (0.098 g, 0.8 mmol) and Eu(NO3)3·6H2O (0.446 g, 1.0 mmol) were added to H4L (0.154 g, 0.2 mmol) in methanol (5 mL). The solution turned red after stirring at room temperature for 3 min. It was sealed and heated at 75 °C for 12 h, then cooled to room temperature over 10 h under a controlled temperature program. Red crystals of 2 were obtained by natural evaporation of the cooled solution in air at room temperature.

properties.summary: Solid-state emission at 77 K (λexc = 360 nm) shows a broad band at 435 nm assigned to intraligand charge transfer in L plus characteristic Eu3+ 5D0 → 7FJ peaks at about 591, 617, 652, and 698 nm. The hypersensitive 5D0→7F2 band is stronger than 5D0→7F1, consistent with the lack of an inversion center at Eu3+.
